description: Creates multiple rate values for a company-level rate table. Returns 207 with per-item status.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the company

parameters.name: rate_table_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the rate table

207.description: Multi-Status: one result per item (201 = created, 409 = labor assignment changed while saving, retry the item, 422 = validation/business error). A labor uniqueness failure is one item 422. error.details[].message remains the JSON payload, and error.details[].meta is that same object: the conflicting rate table, work classification, rate column, and overlapping window. Other items still succeed. On the shared all-flat staging save, a 409 applies to every item in that transaction and nothing in it is written. On a mixed-column request, a 409 applies only to that item; other items can be 201 and are committed.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

value.description: Rate value (must be zero or positive)

condition.description: Condition object containing resource-specific fields. For LABOR rate tables: { work_classification_id: string }. For EQUIPMENT rate tables: { equipment_type_id: string }. For MATERIAL rate tables: ...
